newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ govt wants key assets in NZ hands - Peters.
newsitem.headline: NZ govt wants key assets in NZ hands - Peters.

text.p: New Zealand Treasurer Winston Peters said on Tuesday that the centre-right coalition government believed control and ownership of key assets should remain in New Zealand hands.
"Let me be clear, this coalition government is not opposed to foreign investment," Peters told an investment conference in Auckland.
"However, we believe in the general principle that the control and ownership of important New Zealand resources and assets should be held by New Zealanders."

Peters said the coalition agreement signed last December had strengthened the national interest provision of the Overseas Investment Act to make it clear that land sales to overseas buyers should result in "substantial and identifiable" benefits to the country.

The agreement also said that strategic assets such as Electricity Corporation of New Zealand, national grid operator Trans Power and New Zealand Post, currently in government ownership, would not be sold.
"These sensible restrictions aside, the government welcomes investment that enhances the national interest," he said.
Peters said the government was committed to reciprocal liberalisation in air services where possible, and was keen to pursue bilateral open skies agreements in the Asia-Pacific region and beyond.
On trade policy, Peters said New Zealand would conduct a tariff review in 1998 on "how to move towards a zero end point under a unilateral domestic tariff reduction programme".
"In reaching a decision on the timing of the reduction programme, we will take into account the progress, the speed and commitment being made by our trading partners," he said.
